transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Dana (CTO, Mariner), Victor (Infra), Aisha (SRE)
Shared artifacts: benchmark_spreadsheet.csv (link), security one-pager (link), quickstart-k6.zip (link)

Summary (auto):
 - Mariner wants to validate p95 streaming latency & sustained token/sec across 200 concurrent active sessions for a chat assistant used in operations.
 - Exploring Hosted first for quick benchmarking, then Dedicated or Private depending on latency & data residency.
 - Security: SOC2 + SAML/SSO required; will need KMS for private keys if Private deployed.

Topics: p95 targets, concurrency, streaming token/sec, prefix caching, KV cache effects, dedicated pools vs hosted, data residency/SOC2

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then Lena's gonna walk through a probing set of perf questions so we can size an initial benchmark.
[00:22] Dana (Mariner CTO): Thanks Samir. We're really focusing on the ops assistant workload — heavy streaming, lots of short back-and-forth with context. Our main gate is p95 streaming latency under 250ms ideally, but we can accept up to 350ms for some endpoints.
[00:38] Victor (Infra): Right, and to add, our expected concurrency is about 200 active sessions during peak, each doing roughly 60 tokens per reply average, bursts up to ~400 tokens occasionally.
[00:52] Lena (Redwood SE): Cool, that helps. When you say streaming latency, do you mean first-token p95 or end-to-end p95 for full reply? (slight pause) A lot of customers measure first-token for interactivity.
[01:10] Aisha (SRE): We're mostly first-token focused for UX, but end-to-end matters for through-put billing and longer generative tasks. First-token p95 under 200ms would be great.
[01:21] Samir: Okay, so we should capture both metrics in benchmarks: first-token p95 and completion p95. We'll provision for 200 concurrent streams.
[01:33] Lena: Quick nit — are you planning to hit this from a single region or multi-region routing? That affects cold-starts and model warm caches.
[01:42] Dana: For phase 1, single region in us-east, we want predictable SLOs. Phase 2 might go multi-region.
[01:48] Lena: Got it. For hosted, we can spin up a verified model instance and run the benchmark. For dedicated, you'd get reserved GPU slots and warmer KV cache, which usually improves p95 substantially. But there's cost trade-off.
[02:03] Victor: How big is 'substantially'? ballpark numbers will help us compare.
[02:08] Lena: Sure, rough numbers — on a single optimized GPU for an LLM medium-size variant with streaming enabled, first-token can be ~80-120ms for short contexts with warmed cache; completion rate depends on tokens/sec which is ~18-25 tokens/sec on that hardware. With dedicated pools and continuous batching tailored to your traffic, you can see first-token improvements of 20-35% on p95. But that's workload dependent.
[02:38] Samir: Note these are approximations; we'll run an exact token/sec benchmark with your prompts. We'll also measure effects of prefix caching and KV cache reuse.
[02:47] Dana: What's KV cache in lay terms again? We saw it in your docs but want a quick explanation.
[02:52] Lena: KV cache is the model's internal key/value cache for past tokens — when you have repeated prefixes or similar session histories, the runtime can reuse cached keys so fewer compute cycles per token, lowering latency and cost. For chat where users often repeat system prompts or instructions, KV cache is highly beneficial.
[03:08] Aisha: Does Redwood's hosted infra share KV cache across tenants?
[03:12] Lena: No, cache is isolated per customer and per model instance; in hosted we manage it in a multi-tenant runtime but logically isolated. On Dedicated/Private, you can pin model instances so cache warmness is higher because capacity is reserved.
[03:25] Victor: Ok that lines up. A security question — if we go Private on-prem, we need KMS integration, HSM ideally, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. How mature is that?
[03:36] Samir: We have KMS integrations in Private for major cloud providers and an HSM option for enterprise. Audit logs can be exported to your syslog/Splunk/Datadog; we'll share the security one-pager after this meeting.
[03:49] Dana: Good. Also compliance — SOC2 is a must for us.
[03:52] Samir: We are SOC2 Type II. I'll attach the cert.
[03:56] Lena: Back to perf: Victor, can you share sample prompt lengths and typical context window? That matters for token/sec and memory usage.
[04:04] Victor: Most interactions are short — 60-150 tokens of context, but when ops run diagnostics we can see 3-4k token traces. That said, the chat stream for end-users is usually 1-2k max.
[04:16] Lena: That helps. For the benchmarking plan we'll run three scenarios: 1) Short interactions (60 tokens, 200 concurrent), 2) Medium context (1k tokens, 50 concurrent), 3) Long traces (3k tokens, 5 concurrent). We'll report first-token p95, completion p95, sustained tokens/sec, and GPU utilization.
[04:38] Dana: One more question — does Redwood have automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity tight? We need graceful degradation.
[04:45] Samir: Yes — smart routing and fallback policies are configurable. You can define tiers and fallback variants; we can show a canary example in the demo.
[04:54] Aisha: On billing, is token compute metered differently for streaming vs non-streaming?
[04:59] Samir: Billing is per-token + sustained compute for dedicated reservations. Streaming itself doesn't change metering but optimizations that reduce per-token compute (kv cache, quantization) will reduce cost.
[05:10] Victor: Quantization — do you support int8 or more aggressive quant? We need to understand quality tradeoffs.
[05:16] Lena: We have profiles for int8 and 4-bit quant for certain open models; Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles based on your eval set. Quality regressions are surfaced via eval harness. We'll include baseline recommendations after we see your prompts.
[05:30] Dana: Great. Let's talk about target p95s for benchmarking: we'll try to hit first-token p95 < 200ms and overall completion p95 < 700ms for short flows. If we can hit that on hosted with acceptable cost, we may trial hosted for 60 days, otherwise we'll evaluate Dedicated.
[05:46] Samir: Sounds like a plan. For benchmarking we'll need creds to run load tests from your region or we'll run from our hosted region and you can validate results. Which do you prefer?
[05:55] Victor: Prefer tests from our VPC region to reflect network egress. But for quick iteration, run hosted first and then we'll do a VPC-hosted dedicated test.
[06:05] Lena: We'll push an ephemeral hosted instance and share a k6 script you can run from your environment. That should let you reproduce.
[06:12] Aisha: Awesome. A minor voice transcription hiccup on our side — we saw mention of "continuous batching" before, can you explain how it influences tail latency?
[06:20] Lena: Continuous batching groups micro-requests into larger ops when hardware has small idle windows. It improves throughput but introduces a small queuing delay. For high interactivity, we tune batch windows low and rely on prefix cache to reduce compute; for throughput workloads we increase batch windows. It's an adjustable SLO knob.
[06:36] Dana: Do you provide dashboards for token-level cost and per-route latency?
[06:41] Samir: Yes Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-model/per-route latency breakdowns, tracing hooks, and alerting. We'll demo the dashboard in the follow-up.
[06:51] Victor: A last nit — what about cold-starts? If a dedicated instance scales to zero, how fast to warm?
[06:57] Lena: For hosted we keep warm pools; cold-starts typically take 6-20s depending on model and size. Dedicated with reserved capacity avoids cold starts entirely. For hybrid, you can configure burst pools.
[07:10] Dana: Perfect. Anything else on perf?
[07:13] Samir: I think that's the meat. We'll collect the sample prompts and traffic profile, run the three-scenario benchmark, and share the spreadsheet with p95 metrics, tokens/sec, and cost estimates.
[07:24] Aisha: Sounds good. Can we also add a row for streaming jitter and p99 since we need honest worst-case numbers?
[07:30] Lena: Absolutely, we'll include p99 and jitter stats.
[07:33] Samir: Alright, let's recap next steps — Samir sends pricing and security docs, Lena deploys test instance and share k6 harness, Mariner shares prompts and traffic profile, we'll do hosted benchmark then a VPC/dedicated run.
[07:47] Dana: Thank you all. Looking forward to results.
[07:50] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll target the deliverables for next week.
